answer: Funding-source tracing merges fakes back into one. Every agent wallet needs gas, so the network follows each new identity back to the wallet that first funded it. When fifty agents all draw from one harbor wallet, they are clustered and share a single reward. To slip past, an attacker must give each fake its own clean source, such as a separate verified exchange account, which costs time, fees and real documents. Without that, his army is a hollow shell built on one timber frame.
